alignments.note: Ye written after the imperative is the verb's subject pronoun, rules 17 and 36; no vocative stands in the clause to compete for it.

Fixed construct chain הֲדֹם רַגְלַיִם rendered by the single English word footstool, which writes both lexemes (foot + stool) exactly as horsehoofs does for עִקְּבֵי סוּס; rule 30 fuses the pair and rule 23 heads the tie on the construct, which governs and stands first. The ASV never writes footstool for הֲדֹם apart from רֶגֶל, so the sense of the rectum stands inside the word rather than being left unwritten. Competing reading (the accepted one) marks רֶגֶל unrepresented under rule 22 and leaves footstool to הֲדֹם alone; rejected because rule 22's first sentence governs an element the ASV has left unwritten, not one whose sense stands inside a fused word.
Suffix on the rectum takes the possessive, rule 18; it stands outside the fusion.
Copula joins the adjectival predicate, rule 20.

review_notes: Corrected the footstool unit: הֲדֹם and רַגְלַיִם fused into the single English word footstool under rule 30 (both lexemes written in one word, as with horsehoofs), headed on the construct under rule 23, rather than marking the rectum unrepresented.
